answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Creating a thousand identities no longer gives an attacker influence for free: each must tie up capital, and detected fakes lose it. The rule works best when audits sample claims unpredictably, so an attacker cannot cheaply echo trusted behavior or hide behind a garden of accounts; pigment can mark each account’s stake tier without substituting for proof of identity.
